scope: Current official-source grant opportunities globally accessible to African applicants; excludes loans, equity and credits. Social-enterprise/nonprofit opportunities are labelled.

candidates.title: Rufford Small Grants for Nature Conservation
candidates.deadline_exact_text: There are no deadlines; applications can be submitted at any time of year.
candidates.amount: Stage-dependent grants up to GBP 7,000 (1st), GBP 8,000 (2nd), GBP 12,000 (Booster), or GBP 18,000 (Completion).
candidates.eligibility: Early-career conservationists (including MSc/PhD/recent graduates) from eligible emerging/developing-economy countries; project must be nature conservation-focused, typically involving threatened species. Payment is made through an eligible NGO/university rather than a personal account.
candidates.entity_type: Individual conservationist with NGO/university fiscal host; nonprofit/conservation project
candidates.geography: Eligible emerging/developing economies, including eligible African countries listed by the Foundation
candidates.open_evidence_quote: There are no deadlines - applications can be submitted at any time of year.
candidates.uncertainty: Not a general SME grant. Confirm country list, fiscal-host requirements and the appropriate staged grant in the live portal before applying.

candidates.title: Pollination Project Seed Grants
candidates.deadline_exact_text: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with a brief closure at year-end.
candidates.amount: Current Impact page says general seed grants up to USD 500; the application-questions page says a maximum of USD 1,000, so verify the amount in the live form.
candidates.eligibility: Individuals, informally organized groups and formally registered not-for-profit organizations anywhere in the world. Early-stage, volunteer-led/no paid staff, charitable projects with total project budget under USD 10,000 and organization budget under USD 50,000; not for personal gain or political campaigns.
candidates.entity_type: Individual, grassroots group or nonprofit; not a conventional for-profit SME
candidates.open_evidence_quote: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with a brief closure at year-end.
candidates.uncertainty: Official pages conflict on the cap (USD 500 versus USD 1,000); use the amount shown in the current application form. English application and referee requirements apply to international applicants.

candidates.title: Global EbA Fund Medium-Size Grants 2026
candidates.deadline_exact_text: Grant Size: each grant up to USD 500,000; Submission Window: 12 October to 16 November 2026.
candidates.amount: Up to USD 500,000 per grant; project duration up to 24 months.
candidates.eligibility: Legally recognized NGOs, INGOs, IGOs, CBOs, Indigenous Peoples' Organizations, universities, research institutes, think tanks, private-sector entities and consortia. Projects must address ecosystem-based adaptation, work in ODA-eligible countries or a permitted global/thematic route, and include local partnerships; governments cannot receive direct funding.
candidates.entity_type: Nonprofit, research institution, consortium or private-sector/social-enterprise partner
candidates.sector: Climate adaptation, ecosystem-based adaptation and nature-based solutions
candidates.geography: Global/thematic or ODA-eligible countries; African ODA-eligible countries qualify
candidates.open_evidence_quote: Grant Size: each grant up to USD 500,000; Submission Window: 12 October to 16 November 2026.
candidates.uncertainty: The official page does not publish a submission timezone; preserve the date-only deadline. Private-sector awards are subject to the public-interest and local-partnership conditions, and the portal controls final eligibility.

candidates.title: REACT 2.0 Regional Digital Innovation Fund for Energy & Climate (DIFEC) - Windows 1 and 2
candidates.funder: Africa Enterprise Challenge Fund (AECF), with Sida REACT 2.0
candidates.deadline_exact_text: The current official window page has a live Apply link but does not state a closing deadline.
candidates.amount: Window 1: USD 150,000-300,000; Window 2: USD 250,000-400,000; milestone-based grants for up to 36 months.
candidates.eligibility: Private for-profit companies with an MVP (Window 1) or commercially deployed/revenue-generating digital innovation (Window 2). Activities must be implemented on the African continent and fit digital distributed renewable energy, clean cooking, productive-use energy, climate or resource-management themes. A 1:1 matching contribution is required; grants are explicitly non-repayable.
candidates.entity_type: African or Africa-market private for-profit SME/venture
candidates.sector: Digital clean energy, climate and resource management
candidates.geography: Africa; an entity outside Africa may apply if it demonstrates credible African market entry and implementation
candidates.open_evidence_quote: Matched, non-repayable grant financing disbursed on a milestone-based basis.
candidates.uncertainty: No competition closing date is shown on the current official page, so this is a live undated application rather than a confirmed rolling call. The 1:1 match may include founder equity, supplier credit or inventory; confirm accepted match sources in Submittable.

candidates.title: Advancing SDG Outcomes Through the Utilization of Lacuna Fund's Open Datasets
candidates.funder: Lacuna Fund / Wellcome Trust; implementing partner ACTS
candidates.deadline_exact_text: Application Deadline: November 13, 2026. The Submittable listing displays 9:00 PM, but its timezone is not labelled.
candidates.amount: Up to USD 30,000 total pool; three awards of up to USD 10,000 each; implementation December 2026-May 2027.
candidates.eligibility: Researchers/research teams headquartered in an LMIC Global South country, including nonprofit organizations, research institutions and for-profit social enterprises/teams. Must have ML/data and SDG-domain capability and use a Lacuna dataset; individuals generally need an institutional sponsor.
candidates.entity_type: Nonprofit, research institution or for-profit social enterprise/team
candidates.sector: Data/AI for societal good across SDG domains (health, agriculture, education, climate, water, energy and others)
candidates.geography: Global South LMICs, with Africa explicitly targeted alongside Latin America and South/Southeast Asia
candidates.open_evidence_quote: Available Funding | Up to USD 30,000 (three awards of up to USD 10,000 each)
candidates.uncertainty: ACTS gives the date but no timezone; the Submittable time is shown without a labelled timezone. The Lacuna page linked from the RFP was unavailable during checking, so use ACTS plus the live Submittable portal.

candidates.title: Creatives For Our Future 2026
candidates.deadline_exact_text: Applications are open from 9 September 2026 00:00 GMT until 9 November 2026 11:59pm GMT.
candidates.amount: EUR 20,000 grant, plus education and mentorship; award paid/announced in Fall 2027.
candidates.eligibility: Individuals or sole proprietors aged 21-30 worldwide, with a creative project using fashion, design, art, architecture or engineering to produce measurable sustainability/SDG outcomes by September 2028. Valid passport and travel eligibility are required for the programme elements.
candidates.entity_type: Individual founder, sole proprietor or wholly owned young creative venture
candidates.sector: Sustainable creative industries and SDG innovation
candidates.open_evidence_quote: The application is open from 9th of September 2026 00:00am GMT until the 9th of November 2026 11:59pm GMT.
candidates.uncertainty: This is not a general established-SME or nonprofit call: age, creative-medium and travel requirements are strict, and the monetary award is for the 2027 cohort rather than immediate operating cash.

candidates.title: 2027 Digital Financial Services Grant - Expression of Interest
candidates.deadline_exact_text: Phase 1 EOI closes Friday, December 11, 2026 at 11:59 pm ET.
candidates.amount: Up to USD 350,000 for up to 18 months; up to three awards. Phase 1 is an expression of interest and selected applicants are invited to Phase 2.
candidates.eligibility: Regulated or regulation-ready credit unions, savings cooperatives, remittance providers, community-based financial institutions and digital-wallet providers integrating or piloting Interledger/Rhyza digital financial services. Applications are global, with priority interest in Colombia and the broader Americas.
candidates.entity_type: Regulated/regulation-ready financial institution or fintech provider
candidates.sector: Digital financial services and financial inclusion
candidates.geography: Global applications welcome; Americas are a stated priority, so African applicants should evidence readiness and local need
candidates.uncertainty: This is only Phase 1 EOI, not the full grant proposal; regulation/readiness and sanctions screening apply. Africa is eligible by the global wording but is not the stated regional priority.

candidates.title: D-Prize Global Competition 2026
candidates.deadline_exact_text: Regular Submission Deadline: 15 November 2026 at midnight PT (Pacific Time); extension: 6 December 2026 at midnight PT after pre-registration.
candidates.amount: Up to USD 20,000 to launch a new organization and run a three-month pilot.
candidates.eligibility: Applicants aged 18+ anywhere may apply; winners must operate in a developing country and distribute a proven poverty-fighting intervention. New for-profit or nonprofit organizations/social enterprises are eligible; existing organizations generally need to be under 18 months old or have raised under USD 30,000.
candidates.entity_type: New nonprofit, for-profit social enterprise or mission-driven organization
candidates.sector: Poverty alleviation through distribution of evidence-based interventions (health, education, agriculture, WASH, livelihoods and related areas)
candidates.geography: Global applicants; implementation must be in a developing country, including African countries
candidates.open_evidence_quote: We provide up to $20,000 USD to support a three-month pilot.
candidates.uncertainty: The regular deadline is stated as midnight PT, but the start/end convention is not specified. The extension requires pre-registration before the regular deadline. Official FAQ describes a grant and does not state repayment or equity; verify the current application packet.
